title: Sell Mineral Rights in Lawrenceville, PA
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Lawrenceville, PA
metaDescription: Lawrenceville, PA sits at the Tioga County border with New York — dry-gas Marcellus on one side, a fracking ban on the other. What that means for you.
heroLead: Lawrenceville sits at the very edge of Tioga County, close enough to New York that the different rules on each side of the state line are hard to miss.
intro: Drive a few miles north of Lawrenceville and you cross into New York, where high-volume hydraulic fracturing has been banned since 2014. Stay on the Pennsylvania side and you're in dry-gas Marcellus territory that's been actively drilled for well over a decade. That contrast isn't trivia — it's part of why land values and lease activity on the Pennsylvania side of this border have stayed meaningfully different from what New York landowners just across the line have experienced.

sections.heading: Border-County Drilling Reality
paragraphs: Tioga County has seen sustained horizontal Marcellus development for years, with Seneca Resources among the operators active in the area. Lawrenceville-area parcels benefit from that track record — there's usually real nearby production data to reference rather than pure speculation.

Families here sometimes ask whether New York's ban could someday extend into Pennsylvania — it's a fair question, but current Pennsylvania law and regulation govern Lawrenceville minerals, and we base any offer on that reality rather than speculation about future rule changes.

sections.heading: What New York's Ban Means (and Doesn't Mean) for You
paragraphs: If you own Pennsylvania minerals near Lawrenceville, New York's fracking ban has no legal effect on your rights — it only applies across the state line. It's mainly relevant as context: it's part of why Pennsylvania border counties like Tioga have absorbed leasing interest that might have otherwise been split with New York acreage.

sections.heading: What We Check Before Any Offer
paragraphs: We confirm your deed, check for any existing lease or unit filed against the parcel through Tioga County records, and look at nearby royalty history. From there we build a range grounded in what's actually documented for the area.

faqs.question: Does being near the New York border limit drilling on my land?
faqs.answer: No — Pennsylvania regulations govern your Tioga County minerals regardless of proximity to the state line; New York's rules don't cross the border.

faqs.question: Has Tioga County been actively drilled?
faqs.answer: Yes, it's remained one of the more consistently developed dry-gas counties in the Marcellus play for over a decade.

faqs.question: What's the first step if I want an offer?
faqs.answer: Send us your deed or parcel information if you have it, and we'll pull the rest of the record from Tioga County to put together a written range.

faqs.question: Do buyers pay differently for border-county land versus interior Pennsylvania acreage?
faqs.answer: Value is set by the specific unit and production history, not by proximity to a state line, so we evaluate Lawrenceville parcels the same way we would anywhere else in Tioga County.
